PREFACE 

It is gratifying to note that the last edition of this work still graces the bookshelf of almost every member of the bar, despite the seventeen years of continual use which it has seen. It gives evidence of the fact that no book of forms for use in Pennsylvania has, or probably ever will, displace this standard work. However, the current of business affairs and the exceptional activity of the legislature during these years have wrought numerous changes. Many old forms have been rendered obsolete, many new precedents have been sanctioned by use. The need of a new edition is apparent. 

The editors have attempted to supply this need. In this they have been greatly assisted by, and desire to express their gratitude to Robert M. Bernstein and 

Henry R. Robins, of the Philadelphia Bar; and to the publisher for the full measure of his gift of time and advice drawn from the deep well of a long and worthy experience with lawyers and law books. 

THE EDITORS. 

January 3, 1930.

The demand of the defendant B. for an issue of law respectfully showeth : 

That on the day of - 

19this defendant presented to the auditor his account. That he has claimed an allowance for his just and lawful commissions, amounting to dollars. That the plaintiff has objected to the allowance of said commissions, and has claimed that because (here state the facts relied upon by plaintiff) the defendant has lost and forfeited all claim to commissions, which facts are not disputed; but defendant denies that upon said facts he has forfeited his commissions. Wherefore, the facts being undisputed, the following question of law has arisen, viz.:

Whether upon the facts above stated the defendant has or has not as matter of law forfeited his right to charge his commissions.

The plaintiff contending that, as matter of law upon said facts, the commissions have been forfeited. 

And the defendant denying this, and contending that, as matter of law upon said facts, the commissions have not been forfeited.

Demand for an Issue of Fact 

To C. D., Esq., the auditor in the above case. 

The demand of the plaintiff A. for an issue of fact respectfully showeth :

That in the settlement of the account produced by the defendant before the auditor in the above case, the defendant has claimed that he paid to the plaintiff the sum of dollars on 9 and in support of said allegation, the defendant has produced a writing purporting to be a receipt from plaintiff to defendant for said sum on said date, and the plaintiff has denied that the defendant paid plaintiff said sum as above claimed by defendant, and plaintiff has further denied that said writing is plaintiff's receipt, and plaintiff has charged that said writing is a forgery. And thereupon a question of fact has arisen, to wit, whether said payment was made and whether said writing is genuine. And the plaintiff further avers that the question thus arising is important and is material to the just determination of the case and to the settlement of said account, and he avers that said payment was not made and that said socalled receipt is a forgery. Wherefore the plaintiff demands that the following issue of fact be certified by the auditor to the court, to wit, did the defendant pay to the plaintiff on the sum of dollars, and is said so-called receipt genuine? 

And the plaintiff demands that said issue be tried by a jury. (Affidavit of plaintiff.)

ACCOUNTS Feigned Issue 

A feigned issue is hereby stated by the above-named parties under the order of court made following question: 

Did B. on pay A. upon the dollars and is the receipt held by B. for said sum genuine?

B. affirms that he did so pay, and that receipt is genuine. 

A. Denies this.

The affirmative of the issue is with B. And the issue is to be tried with same effect as if a Narr. in feigned issue had been filed setting forth a discourse, wager, etc., and a plea thereto had been filed admitting the wager, but denying plaintiff's averments, all in the usual form.

Signatures of parties. 

Signatures of counsel.

ACCOUNTS See DECEDENTS' ESTATES, as to procedure relating to accounts.

Forms are given for the accounts of Executors, Administrators, Trustees, Guardians and Assignees.

Accounts of Executors and Administrators and final accounts of Guardians are filed in the office of the Register of Wills and must be advertised. Accounts of Testamentary Trustees are filed in the Orphans' Court, as are the triennial accounts of guardians.

Accounts of Executors and Administrators should be filed six months after the advertising of the grant of Letters. Guardians are obliged to file accounts for inspection every three years. 

The final account of a guardian should cover the entire period of the guardianship.

It is essential that there be no blending of principal and income, administration and distribution or realty and personalty. 

Real estate if appearing in an account should, as a general rule. be the subject of separate statement.

ADMINISTRATOR 

11 When separate Orphans' Courts exist, such accounts as properly come before them are audited by the court; in other counties an auditor may be appointed. 

The court will not audit an account or decree a distribution until six months has expired after the grant of letters.

Acknowledgments.—Within the state may be made at any place within the state before a justice or clerk of the supreme court, or judge of a superior court, or within the city, county, or township for which the officer was elected or appointed, a court commissioner, notary public, or a justice of the peace, a clerk of a court of record, or a county recorder.

Without the state, before a justice, judge, or clerk of any court of record of the United States, a justice, judge or clerk of any court of record of any state, a commissioner appointed by the governor of this state for that purpose, a notary public, or any other officer of the state where the acknowledgment is made, authorized by its laws to take such proof or acknowledgment. 

Without the United States, before a minister, commissioner, or chargé d'affaires of the United States, resident and accredited in the country where the proof or acknowledgment is made, or, a consul, vice-consul or consular agent of the United States, resident in the country where the proof or acknowledgment is made; or a judge of a court of record of the country, where the proof or acknowledgment is made; or commissioners appointed for such purposes by the governor of this state, pursuant to special statutes; or a notary public. Where any of the foregoing officers are permitted to appoint deputies, such deputies may act in the name of the principal.

When not acknowledged, proof may be made, by the parties executing the instrument or either of them; by a subscribing witness; or by proof of the handwriting of the party and of a subscribing witness, where the parties are dead, nonresidents, &c.

CONNECTICUT 

Acknowledgments.-Within the state, before a judge of a court of record of this state or of the United States; a clerk of the superior court, court of common pleas, or district court, justice of the peace, commissioner of the school fund, commissioner of the superior court, notary public, either with or without his official seal, town clerk, or assistant town clerk.

Conveyances of real estate situated in this state and powers of attorney therefor, executed and acknowledged in any other state or territory in conformity with its laws relative to the conveyance of lands therein situated, shall be valid.

All conveyances of the real estate of wives married prior to April 20, 1877, which are executed by them jointly with their husbands, and duly acknowledged and recorded, shall be valid and effectual to transfer such estate; and all conveyances, by the husband alone, of the real estate of such a wife, shall be ineffectual to convey her interest therein, but no joinder by the husband shall be required in case of a wife married on or after said date. On the death of a husband or wife married on or

ACKNOWLEDGMENTS 

after the 20th day of April, 1877, the survivor shall be entitled to the use for life of one-third in value of all property real and personal, legally or equitably owned by the other at the time of his or her death, after the payment of all debts and charges against the estate. The right to such third shall not be defeated by any disposition of the property by will, to other parties, but where there is no will, the survivor shall take such third absolutely. Husband and wife must nevertheless join in conveyance of homestead.

Without the state, before any consul-general, consul, vice-consul, consular agent, or commercial agent of the United States duly appointed in any foreign country, at the places of their respective official residences, before any judge of any district court of the United States, or the chancellor, or any judge of a court of record of any state, territory or country, or the mayor or chief officer of any city or borough, and certified under the hand of such chancellor, judge, mayor or officer, and the seal of his office, court, city, or borough, or in any such court, and certified under the hand of the clerk or other officer of said court, and the seal of said court, or a commissioner of deeds appointed by the governor, or a notary public of any state, territory, or district. 

Dower and curtesy exist. Husband and wife should join for the purpose of releasing dower and curtesy; the wife being examined separate and apart from her husband.

Acknowledgments.-Within the state, before a judge of a court of record, justice of the peace, notary public, or clerk of the superior court. The three last act only in the county for which they were appointed.

ACKNOWLEDGMENTS 

Without the state, before a commissioner of deeds for Georgia, a consul or vice-consul of the United States (the certificates of these officers under their seal being evidence of the fact), a judge of a court of record in the state where executed, with a certificate of the clerk under the seal of such court of the genuineness of the signature of such judge, a clerk of a court of record under the seal of the court, or a notary public of the state and county where executed, with his seal of office attached. 

If the notary has no seal, his official character must be certified by a clerk of any court of record in the county of the notary's residence.

Joinder by the wife is unnecessary except where the title to the lands conveyed is derived through her. 

The form of acknowledgment used in the state where the deed or other instrument is executed is sufficient as a prerequisite to recording if one of the witnesses be the officer before whom it is taken, attested by his seal of office or, if he have no seal, a certificate by a clerk of a court of record be annexed. If, however, it be not made in this manner it may be proved before such an officer in the following form by a subscribing witness or the maker:

Acknowledgments.-Within the territory, before the registrar of conveyances, or his deputy or a judge of a court of record, or notary public. 

Without the territory, before any officer of any of the states authorized to take proofs or acknowledgments of deeds, accompanied however by a certificate of the clerk of a court of record of the authority of such officer.

The person offering to make such acknowledgment must be personally known to the officer taking the same to be the person whose name is subscribed to such conveyance as a party thereto, or shall be proved to be such by the oath or affirmation of a credible witness known to the officer.

Dower and curtesy. Husband and wife are each entitled to one-third of the lands of the other for life. 

Dower may be barred by the wife joining in the deed or by separate deed of release.

Married women have the same control of their property as if sole, but they may not mortgage or sell real estate without the written consent of their husbands.

ILLINOIS 

Acknowledgments. Within the state, before a master in chancery, notary public under his seal, United States commissioner under his seal, county clerk, justice of the peace of the county where the lands lie, any court of record having a seal, or judge, justice or clerk thereof, attested by the seal of the court. 

Without the state, before a justice of the peace, notary public, master in chancery, United States commissioner, commissioner of deeds, mayor of a city, clerk of a county, any judge, justice, clerk, or deputy clerk of the supreme, circuit, superior, district, county, common pleas, probate, orphans' or surrogate's court in conformity with the laws of the state where made; a certificate of authority by the clerk of a court of record being attached. A certificate of authority should be attached where taken by a justice of the peace, or master in chancery. If taken by the mayor of a city it must be under the city seal and if by a clerk or other officer of the court, under the seal of that court.

Without the United States, before any court having a seal, any judge, justice or clerk thereof, notary public, commissioner, ambassador, minister, secretary of legation, consul, vice-consul, deputy consul, commercial or consular agent of the United States in any foreign country, attested by his official seal, or before any officer authorized by the laws of such place having a seal. Such acknowledgments should be certified by a consul or other

Dower, strictly speaking, does not exist though a wife has a lien against her husband's property to secure moneys received by him for her account, which lien or mortgage, as well as any other rights she may have in real estate, she may release.

A married woman cannot sell or mortgage her property without her husband's consent. The latter can sell or mortgage his own without joinder of wife.

ACQUITTANCE SEE RECEIPTS; RELEASE 

An acquittance is an agreement in writing to discharge a party from an engagement to pay a sum of money; it is evidence of payment. It differs from a release in this, that the latter must be under seal, while an acquittance is not under seal. In 

Pennsylvania a receipt, though not under seal, has nearly the same effect as a release. But if not under seal it is necessary to show the consideration thereof. See Act of 1927, P. L. 985.

ADMIRALTY The Constitution of the United States, Art. 111, Sec. 1, states that "The judicial power (of the United States) shall extend to all cases, in law and equity arising under this. Constitution, ....; to all cases of Admiralty and Maritime Jurisdiction." 

1. Libel in Rem for Collision The L. & M. Steamship Company, a corporation, VS. Libellant. 

The K. & R. Steamship Company, a corporation, Respondent.

In Admiralty. 

To the Honorable, the Judges of the United States Dis trict Court, for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania: 

The libel and complaint of the L. & M. Company, owner of the steamship Bailey, against the steamship Reyburn, her engines, tackle, apparel, etc., and against all persons intervening for their interest in the same, in a cause of collision, civil and maritime, alleges as follows: 

1. At all the times hereinafter mentioned, the L. & M. 

Steamship Company was and is a corporation, and the owner of the steamship Bailey.. 

2. The steamship Reyburn herein proceeded against, is now, or during the currency of process herein, will be, within the port of Philadelphia, and within the jurisdiction of this Honorable Court.

ADMIRALTY 

of 

3. On Wednesday, the 

1929, at about four o'clock P. M. a collision occured between the steamship Bailey and Reyburn, on the high seas, about a mile and a half southwest of Cape May, N. J., by reason of which the Bailey sustained severe damage. 

4. Upon information and belief, the libellant alleges that the following are the circumstances of the collision: [Describe circumstances of collision in detail]. 

5. Libellant alleges that the collision and consequent damage was in no way due to any fault on the part of the steamship Bailey which was in all respects properly and carefully managed and navigated, but due to the fault of the steamship Reyburn in the following amongst other particulars which will be pointed out on the trial of this action: (a) In that she was navigated at too great speed in a fog. (b) In that she did not give proper heed to the signals of the Bailey. (c) In that she did not stop and reverse her engines in time as she should have done. (d) In that she did not have a proper and efficient lookout. (e). In that her master and officers were incompetent and inattentive to their duties. (f) In that she was equipped with turbine engines which could not be reversed in time to prevent the collision. (g) In that she failed to stop when the fog signals of the Bailey were first heard. 

6. Libellant further alleges by reason of said collision he has suffered damages to the steamship Bailey with her cargo, and on account of the expenses arising out of said collision, in a sum which libellant is at present, unable to state with accuracy, but which, upon information and belief, will amount to one hundred thousand ($100,000) dollars.

AFFIDAVITS AND OATHS 

Forms of affidavits and oaths in various proceedings and of various officers, etc., will be found under the appropriate titles. 

An affidavit is an oath or affirmation reduced to writing, sworn or affirmed to before some officer who has authority to administer it. It differs from a deposition in this, that, in the latter, the opposite party has had an opportunity to cross-examine the witness, whereas an affidavit is always taken ex parte. 

An oath is an outward pledge, given by the person taking it, that his attestation or promise is made under an immediate sense of his responsibility to God. Greenleaf on Ev. 328. 

Oaths are taken in various forms: a usual form is upon the 

Gospel, by taking the book in hand; and the words commonly used are, "You do swear that," &c., "so help you God," and then kissing the book. The origin of this oath may be traced to the Roman law; and the kissing the book is said to be in imitation of the priest's kissing the ritual, as a sign of reverence, before he reads it to the people. Rees' Cycl.

In Pennsylvania, by Act of 3d April, 1895, P. L. 32, 3 Purd. 

3335, laying the hand upon an open copy of the Holy Bible is substituted for the old form of kissing the book. 

Another form is by the witness or party promising, holding up his right hand while the officer repeats to him "You do swear by Almighty God, the Searcher of all Hearts, that," &c., "and that as you shall answer to God at the last great day."

In another form of attestation, commonly called an affirmation, the officer repeats, "You do solemnly, sincerely, and truly declare and affirm, that," &c., "And so you affirm," or, "are you content?" The oath may, however, be varied in any other form, in order to conform to the religious opinions of the person who takes it. 

The act of 23 April, 1909, P. L. 140, 5 Purd. 5810-11, provides that the capacity of any witness to testify in any judicial proceeding shall be in no wise affected by his opinion on matter of religion; that no witness shall be questioned concerning his religious belief nor any evidence be heard on the subject; and that the affirmation may be administered to any witness who so desires, and shall have the same effect as the oath. 

Form of Oath by Kissing or Laying the Hand upon the 

Book 

Yo do swear, that 

So help you God.

Form of Oath by Lifting up the Right Hand 

You do swear by Almighty God, the Searcher of all 

Harts, that and that as you shall answer to God at the last Great Day.

Form of Affirmation You do slomenly, sincerely, and truly declare and affirm, that ; and so you affirm.

In the forms which follow, the first blank space should be filled, according to the mode of administering an oath or affirmation, as follows, viz:

If an oath by kissing or laying the hand upon the Book, fill with "swear."

If an oath by kissing or laying the hand upon the Book, fill with "So help you God."

If anoath by uplifted hand, fill with "and that as you shall answer to God at the last Great Day.' 

If an affirmation, fill with "and so you affirm."

I have not paid or contributed or promised to pay or

AFFIDAVIT OF DEFENSE SEE: STATEMENTS OF CLAIM-JUDGMENTS-PARTICULAR FORMS OF ACTION 

The Practice Act of 14 May, 1915, P. L. 483, has superseded all acts regulating practice in assumpsit and trespass as defined in the Act of 1887, P. L. 271. Section 12 requires that "the defendant shall file an affidavit of defense to the statement of claim within fifteen days from service thereof." Counties, cities, boroughs, etc., need not do so by virtue of the Act of 1917, P. L. 

150. Affidavits must contain and contain only the material facts relied upon, set forth in a concise and summary form. 

Since the sufficiency of affidavits of defense is nearly always a matter of substantive law, it is obviously impossible to give anything like a complete collection of forms of affidavits. A few typical forms are appended which may be found useful as guides.

Particular Affidavits

In the following forms the caption, commencement, conclusion and jurat are to be supplied.

Denial of Execution of Note 

Deponent denies that on the day of 19, or any other day was he the maker of the four (4) certain promissory notes for dollars each which are set forth in plaintiff's statement of claim filed in this cause.

Deponent further alleges that he did not authorize the signing of the said notes or either of them by any one in his behalf, nor did he ratify the signing of any of said notes or either of them by any one in his behalf, and he further alleges that he is not indebted to the said plaintiff in any sum whatever on account of the four (4) certain promissory notes or either of them sued upon in this action.

Parol Inducing Agreement

Goods Sold and Delivered; Defective Quality; Rescission

The defendants thereupon gave to the plaintiff's said agent, an order for nineteen pieces of gray mixed worsted goods, being the goods mentioned in the plaintiff's statement of claim. The said order for the said goods was given by the defendants in reliance upon the said sample, it being expressly agreed that the said goods were to be like the said sample in every respect and the plaintiff warranted that the said goods would be perfect, fully equal to the said sample and suitable for the purpose for which they were ordered as above mentioned. 

The defendants further allege that in an alleged fulfillment of the said order the plaintiff shipped nineteen (19) pieces of gray mixed worsted goods to the defendant in 19, as alleged in the statement of plaintiff's claim, but the defendants deny that the said merchandise was of good merchantable quality, but the defendants allege that the said goods were unmerchantable, were not perfect, were not suited for the purpose of

manufacturing ladies' suits, and were not in accordance with the sample, nor up to the sample, but on the contrary, the said goods were unmerchantable, unsuited to the said purpose, imperfect, and that "runners" were found all through the said goods. The defendants further allege that "runners" are heavy threads running through the goods which result from imperfections in weaving and render the goods in question unmerchantable and entirely unsuited for the purpose for which the order was given as aforesaid. The defendants further allege that the said goods were dirty, not in the ordinary sense but in the technical trade sense, that is to say the goods were not of the right color, were not the color of the sample, and were for that reason alone entirely unsuited for use in the manufacture of ladies' suits in filling orders which the defendants had on hand for said suits when the said order was given to the plaintiff. 

The defendants further allege that a few days after receiving the said goods they inspected the same and found thereby that the goods were imperfect and defective as above alleged. Thereupon the defendants returned the said goods to the plaintiff for the season above set forth and made such re-delivery unconditionally and the plaintiff accepted the return of all of the said goods. During the few days in which the goods remained in the possession of the defendants no change was made in them and the defendants exercised no right of ownership in them whatever, and when they were returned as aforesaid to the plaintiff they were in the same condition in which the defendants received them. 

The defendants allege that they are not indebted to the plaintiff for any sum whatever in respect to the said goods or because of any alleged loss by reason of a resale at less than the contract price. The defendants further allege that the said goods had no market value for the defendants' purposes at the time of their delivery to defendants.

(Follow General Form as in Affidavit of Defense.)  SEE LETTERS OF CREDIT AND GUARANTEES; MARRIAGE, AS TO ARTICLES OF SEPARATION; PARTNERSHIP; SURETY; ARBI- TRATION AND REFERENCE 

A CONTRACT is an agreement, upon sufficient consideration, to do or not to do a particular thing. If under seal, it is denominated a specialty, and if not under seal, an agreement by parol;

and the latter includes verbal and written contracts not under seal.

In effect, there is little difference between an agreement in writing without a seal, and one by parol; except that the former can be more easily proved, and is, therefore, to be preferred. 

While not absolutely necessary, it is, in most cases, desirable that written contracts should be under seal. 

Care should be taken to have the agreement or contract clearly understood and expressed. The want of care, is a fruitful source of difficulty and lawsuits.

To render an agreement complete, six things must concur; there must be, 1st, a person to contract; 2d, a person able to be contracted with; 3d, a thing to be contracted for; 4th, a lawful consideration; 5th, clear and explicit words to express the agreement; and 6th, the assent of the contracting parties. Consideration is no longer necessary in a written release or promise if there is an additional express statement that the signer intends to be legally bound. Act of May 13, 1927. P. L. 985.

C. Agreement of Adjoining Land Owners Whereunder 

One is Permitted to Erect a Party Wall, One-half on 

Each Parcel of Ground.

THIS AGREEMENT made the day of 

A. D. 

19by the J. D. (herein called the 1st party) and R. R. (herein called the 2d party.) 

WITNESSETH:- 

WHEREAS the first party is the owner of the premises situated (description). 

AND WHEREAS, the second party is the owner of premises adjoining the aforesaid premises and described as follows: (description). 

AND WHEREAS, the first party is about to erect a building on his aforesaid premises; 

AND WHEREAS, it has been agreed that the wall of said building shall be a party wall, and shall be constructed

and erected, to the extent of ½ of its thickness upon the aforesaid land of each party :— NOW THEREFORE IT IS MUTUALLY AGREED, 1. That the said wall so to be constructed by the First 

Party shall be used and maintained as a party wall forever. 

2. That the First Party shall be permitted, freely and without interference, or hindrance, to enter upon the parcel of land of the Second Party, for the purpose of excavating and constructing the said party wall. 

3. That the said party wall so to be constructed shall not extend nearer the street than the front wall of the building on the easterly side of said parcel of land, from which point it may be extended northerly for a distance not exceeding fifty-five (55) feet; that the party wall so to be constructed shall be laid on good and sufficient bottom stone, which shall be bedded not less than nine (9) feet below the curbstone in front of the dividing line between the said parcels of land; that the foundation of said wall so to be constructed shall be made and constructed of good stone, and shall be not less than twentyfour (24) inches in thickness to the underside of the first tier beams; that, above the underside of the first tier beams, it shall be made and constructed of sound hard brick and shall be not less than sixteen (16) inches in thickness all the way up to the roof of the building of the First Party; and that it shall be extended and constructed to a proper height above the roof of such building, and shall be covered with a proper coping of blue stone. 

4. That, whenever the Second Party shall desire to use said party wall, the Second Party shall pay such proportion of the value of said wall as the portion thereof, which he may use, shall bear to the value of the whole of said wall, and such value shall be ascertained, in the event of a disagreement in respect thereof between the parties, by arbitration; and each party, in the event of

PARTY WALLS 

205 such disagreement, shall choose one disinterested person. 

If those chosen shall be unable to agree, they shall choose a third person to aid in ascertaining and fixing such valuation, and a decision of any two of such persons, shall be binding upon both parties. 

5. That, if either party shall, at any time, desire to raise said wall to a greater height than that to which it may at first be carried, he shall be at liberty to do so, and such additional wall shall be made and constructed by such party wholly at his expense, unless the other party shall desire to use the whole, or any portion, of such additional wall; and, in such a case, such other party shall pay for the same in the manner above provided for the main wall. 

6. That, if it shall be necessary, at any time, to repair, or rebuild, the whole, or any portion, of said wall, the expense of such repairing, or rebuilding, shall be borne equally between the said parties as to such portions of such wall as shall be used in common by them, and the cost of repairing, or rebuilding, the remaining portion thereof shall be borne wholly by the party, who may exclusively use the same. 

7. That, whenever said wall shall be repaired, or rebuilt, it shall occupy the same space and shall be of the same, or similar, materials, and of the same size, as the present wall, unless any law, or laws, hereafter in force and effect, shall require a wall of different dimensions; and in such event, such wall, when so repaired, or rebuilt, shall be of the dimensions required by such law or laws. 

8. That nothing in this agreement contained shall be deemed to vest in either party any part of the fee of the soil upon which the said party wall shall stand. 

9. That this agreement shall be perpetual, and shall bind the parties hereto, and their respective heirs, administrators and assigns.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have hereunto set their hands and seals, the day and year first above written.

Conditions of Contract [Annexed to Preceding Contract] 

The Contractor to whom this work shall be awarded, agrees to and with the Owner as follows: 

1. That he and his subcontractors will execute the works in accordance with the following specifications and the drawings to which they refer. 

2. That he will accept the said specifications and drawings as a whole, and not separately, because they are intended to illustrate and explain each other; that he will construe the written notes on drawings as specifications, and will check and verify all written and scale dimensions.

3. That he will make and submit shop-drawings of construction for the inspection and approval of the Architects, and will illustrate carvings by satisfactory models or photographs. 

4. That he will provide all materials (including water), all implements, scaffolding, transportation, and labor necessary to construct and complete the works described by the said drawings and specifications. 

5. That the materials will be the best of the kind called for, and the workmanship done with the best art and skill in each trade. 

6. That he will begin the works and completely finish and deliver them in the time and on the conditions hereinafter named in the specifications and contract. 

7. That he will keep at all times a competent representative upon the works. 

8. That he will insure and keep insured the building in amounts and companies approved by Owner; policies to be made payable to Owner and Contractor as their interests may appear. 

9. That he will pay for Building and Highway permits, and will comply with Building Laws and Ordinances, and Board of Health Regulations. 

10. That during the performance of this contract he will defend and keep the Owner indemnified from suits, claims and demands, and from damages of all description done to persons or property in the course of operations under and by reason of this contract, and also from all suits growing out of alleged infringments of patents, or out of the use of patented appliances. 

11. That he shall remain an "independent contractor," with the legal results of such relation to the Owner. 

12. That he will make changes from original drawings and specifications, as shall be requested by the Owner, without any claim for vitiation of his contract; and that no charge will be made by him for such changes, except they be ordered in writing by the Owner.

THIS AGREEMENT, made and concluded this , A. D. 19between day of the City of Philadelphia, in the State of Pennsylvania, owner, builder, hereinafter called the party of the first part, and whose address is of the said City, Contractor, hereinafter called the party of the second part. 

WHEREAS, The said party of the first part as owner in fee of the lot or piece of ground below mentioned and referred to is about to erect thereon fifty two-story dwellings, situate [description] according to certain drawings, plans and specifications (hereinafter called "specifica-

tions") which are made part of this contract and are to be deposited with the West End Trust Company, Broad Street and South Penn Square, Philadelphia, Pa., identified by the signatures of the parties hereto thereon. 

AND WHEREAS, The West End Trust Company, through having no interest in the lot of ground above described or the buildings to be erected thereon, has, at the request of the parties hereto, made or is about to make certain insurances of completion and against liens, and as a condition for so doing has required the execution of this present contract.

NOW THIS AGREEMENT WITNESSETH, that the said party of the second part for the consideration hereinafter mentioned and referred to, hereby covenants and agrees with the party of the first part, in a good and workman-like manner, and according to the said drawings, plans and specifications and the terms of this contract, to the satisfaction of the party of the first part, and the Trust Company aforesaid, to do and perform all of the work mentioned and referred to in Schedule "A," and to furnish and supply all the labor and materials mentioned and referred to in said schedule necessary for the proper performance of the said work which the party of the second part has undertaken to do, as set forth, mentioned and referred to in Schedule "A" hereto annexed and made part of this contract.

The party of the first part in consideration of the true and faithful performance by the party of the second part of the covenants and agreements herein contained or mentioned and referred to on his part to be kept and observed and done and performed, hereby covenants and agrees with the party of the second part to pay to sum or sums of money and other consideration mentioned and specified, and in the manner and form set forth in Schedules "B" and "C" hereto annexed and made part of this contract.

The party of the second part shall, upon request from the party of the first part, furnish forthwith to the party

Trust Company; in the sum of dollars, conditioned for the true and faithful performance of this contract on the part of the party of the second part. 

The party of the second part, for himself, herself, itself, themselves, his, her, its and their subcontractors, and all parties acting through or under him, it or them, covenants and agrees that no mechanics' claims or liens shall be filed or maintained by him, them or any of them against the said buildings and the lots of ground appurtenant thereto, or any of them, for or on account of any work done or materials furnished by him, them or any of them, under this contract or otherwise, for, towards, in or about the erection and construction of the said buildings, or any of them, and the party of the second part, for himself, herself, itself, themselves, his, her, its and their subcontractors and others under him, her, it or them, hereby expressly waives and relinquishes the right to have, file or maintain any mechanics' lien or claim against the said buildings or any of them, and that this agreement waiving the right of lien shall be an independent cnvenant. 

That the party of the second part shall be considered an independent contractor in respect of that part of the work in the erection and construction of the said buildings which he has undertaken to do and perform, and that he shall alone be answerable for any loss or damage caused by himself or his subcontractors, agents or employees, and he agrees to fully indemnify, protect and save harmless the party of the first part against loss, damage or expense as to all claims or liabilities resulting from accident, negligence, or from other cause. 

That party of the second part promises and agrees to furnish the materials which he has undertaken to supply, promptly, and to push the work vigorously, without any delays, with such force of mechanics and workmen as

shall be satisfactory to the party of the first part and said Trust Company aforesaid, and so as not to delay or hinder the other mechanics engaged upon the premises, and if the party of the second part, at any time during the progress of the said work, shall, in the opinion of the party of the first part, or of the said Trust Company, refuse, omit or neglect to furnish and supply a sufficiency. the second part remains in default, in the opinion of the party of the first part, or of the Trust Company aforesaid, to procure in the market the materials required, and to secure the necessary number of workmen and mechanics to carry forward the said work, upon the credit and for the account of the party of the first part, and to charge the cost and expense thereof to the party of the second part, and against any balance payable in cash or otherwise that may be then or thereafter become due to the party of the second part for or on account of or under this contract, and the party It is hereby expressly declared and agreed between the parties hereto, that the said Trust Company; is hereby authorized and empowered to give all the notices mentioned in the preceding section, to purchase all the materials, and to procure all labor that may, in their judgment and discretion, be required to complete the operation in the same manner that the party of the first part might or has the right or power to do, and further, that the said Trust Company shall also have the right, power and authority in the name of the party of the first part, and without liability for so doing, to cancel this contract, and in the name and for the account of the party of the first part or his heirs, executors or administrators, to make other contracts, and to procure other labor and materials, or either, which, in the judgment and discretion of them, or either of them, may be deemed necessary to complete the said houses, shall also have the power and authority, in the name of the party of the first part, or to the use of the said Trust Company, to retain from any money held by the said Trust Company, or otherwise, for the benefit of the said party of the second part, or to demand and recover from the party of the second part, the cost and expense of the completion of the contract of the party of the second part, if the cost and expense thereof shall be in excess of any money that would otherwise have been payable to the party of the second part, if he had fulfilled his contract according to its terms.

It is further declared and agreed by and between the parties hereto, that any and all notices to proceed with

the work or to cancel contracts, and any and all contracts of employment, or for material, or for labor, or completion, made by the Trust Company shall be binding upon the parties hereto, their heirs, executors, administrators and assigns, with like force and effect as though originally made by the party of the first part or for the account of the party of the first part, and if the Trust Company shall give any notices, herein empowered or authorized to be given, or if any work or labor or materials are contracted for by the said Trust Company; aforesaid, for the operation aforesaid, or if any notice of cancellation of this contract is given to the party of the second part by the Trust Company aforesaid, in any capacity, then the parties hereto agree that any notices, orders or directions thereafter given or attempted to be given by the party of the first part, without being accompanied by the written approval of the said Trust Company, shall be inoperative, and without any binding force, virtue or effect between the parties to this agreement. 

The remedies herein provided shall be in addition to and not in substitution for the rights and remedies which would otherwise be vested in the party of the first part, or in the said Trust Company aforesaid, under the terms of the agreement or otherwise, all of which rights and remedies are specially reserved by the party of the first part; and the failure to exercise the remedies herein provided shall not preclude the resort to any other appropriate remedy; nor shall the use of the special remedies hereby provided prevent the subsequent or concurrent resort to any other remedy which by law would be vested in the party of the first part for the recovery of damages or otherwise in the event of a breach of any of the covenants by the party of the second part. 

The said party of the first part shall not in any manner be answerable or accountable for any loss or damage that shall or may happen to the said work, or any part thereof, or to any of the materials or other things done,

It is understood and agreed that no extra charge or claim shall be made for any work done upon, or for materials furnished or supplied for the said buildings, whether called for in this contract or not, unless an agreement with respect thereto shall have been first reduced to writing and signed by the parties hereto, and be approved by the said Trust Company, and when extra work or materials are so ordered, the agreement in reference to the same shall be considered a separate and distinct contract, in no way altering or affecting the terms of this contract, the amount agreed upon to be paid in the same way and manner and subject to the same terms and conditions (including the waiver of the right of lien) as have been made as to the payment of the original contract price, unless otherwise agreed in writing.

It is agreed that all materials delivered upon the said premises shall be regarded as the property of the said party of the first part, and shall not be removed without his consent in writing. The said party of the second part shall not sublet any part of this contract. 

It is further expressly understood and agreed that the work and labor to be done and performed, and the materials to be furnished, supplied and delivered, or either, by the party of the second part, shall, in all respect, agree and comply with the requirements in the "specifications" first above mentioned and referred to contained; provided, however, and it is further understood and agreed that if the requirements and specifications in respect thereto, as set forth in Schedule "A," shall vary from the requirements mentioned and set forth in said “specifications" first above mentioned and referred to, then the said requirements and specifications, as contained and set forth in Schedule "A" shall govern, but so far only as they shall be a substitute for the requirements and specifications set forth and contained in the said "specifications" first above mentioned and referred to. The other

parts and portions of the said "specifications" not covered by the provisions in Schedule "A" shall remain in as full force and effect as if no change had been made, and shall be accordingly followed, observed and complied with.

If the said party of the second part shall fail, neglect or refuse to proceed with the performance of this contract in the manner and according to the terms and conditions thereof, as required from time to time, and the party of the first part, or the said Trust Company aforesaid, shall proceed to hire other contractors and other mechanics, and to purchase other materials, or either or any of the same, in order to proceed with or complete the work agreed to be done or the materials agreed to be supplied hereunder, then it is agreed that any securities, mortgages, real estate or equities held to secure any payments agreed to be made hereunder to the party of the second part, shall, at the option and in the discretion of the party of the first part, the said Trust Company aforesaid, or either or any of them, be sold and disposed of either at public or private sale, for the best price that the same may be sold for or disposed of, in the judgment and discretion of the party of the first part, and the Trust Company aforesaid, or either or any of them, and the proceeds thereof shall be held and disposed of to pay for any work done or materials supplied to complete, finish and perform the work agreed to be done or the materials agreed to be supplied hereunder. Nothing, however, contained in this paragraph shall impose any duty or obligation upon the party of the first part, the Trust Company, or either or any of the same, to dispose of any of the securities or property so held. If the party of the second part shall pay for such work and labor and materials or either of the same, as may be ordered or purchased by the party of the first part, or the said Trust Company; aforesaid, then the said moneys shall be paid over to the party of the second part less any costs, charges, commissions, counsel fees, interests or damages sustained by the party

It is hereby futher mutually covenanted, promised and agreed, by and between the said parties, that in the event of any dispute or disagreement hereafter arising between them as to the character, style or portion of the work on said buildings to be done, or materials to be furnished under this contract, or the plans and specifications hereinbefore referred to, or any other matter in connection herewith, the same shall be referred to three arbitrators, one to be chosen by each of the parties hereto, and the third by the two arbitrators so selected, whose decision, or that of a majority of them in the matter, shall be final and binding upon them.

It is hereby expressly declared and agreed between the parties hereto, that the Trust Company aforesaid or the Trustee mentioned in Schedule "B" or "C" hereinbefore mentioned to hold title to the securities, mortgages, real estate or equities held to secure any payments agreed to be made hereunder, shall not be held liable for the delivery of such securities, mortgages, real estate or equities as aforesaid, or for the title to such securities, mortgages, real estate or equities as represented in this agreement, unless said Trust Company or Trustee shall undertake so to do in writing duly executed; nor shall the said Trust Company or Trustee aforesaid, in any way or manner become liable for any liens, taxes, claims, interest on encumbrances or other charges, that have or may accrue against the said securities, mortgages, real estate or equities as aforesaid, and may deliver such securities, mortgages, title to real estate or equities when and if in their discretion the same may become due to the said party of the second part, without any further order or authority for so doing. This direction being their sufficient warrant.

It is expressly covenanted and agreed by the parties hereto, that upon the faith of the provisions of this agreement, including the waiver of the right of lien, the

Trust Company. And should any such contract or any changes in "specifications" (anything in said "specifications" to the contrary notwithstanding), have been or be hereafter made in violation hereof, the same shall be null and void, so far as the same may in any way affect the said premises above described or subject the same to lien, or in any way affect the said Trust Company, and any liability incurred by said Trust Company upon the faith hereof. So that no matter or thing heretofore or hereafter occurring or happening between the owner or contractor shall ever lessen or impair the full force and effect of this contract, and especially the contractors' independent covenant and agreement not to file liens as herein set forth.

And it is further understood, covenanted and agreed that the said Trust Company is in no way whatever liable to either of the parties hereto for the performance of any act, matter or thing to be done or performed by either of the said parties, or for the failure of either of said parties to keep and perform any of the covenants hereof, nor shall said Trust Company be responsible or liable to either of said parties for any matter or thing connected. with this contract or said building operation, excepting in so far as said Trust Company shall have undertaken, in writing duly executed, to assume or undertake such obligations to the said parties.

consideration of the further sum of dollars, to be paid by the said William Burns, as hereinafter is mentioned, hath granted, bargained, and sold, and by these presents doth grant, bargain, and sell, unto the said William Burns, his executors, administrators, and assigns, one hundred of the oak trees, now standing and growing in and upon the farm called Brookland, in the county of now in the tenure of John Jay, which the said William Burns shall think fit to choose, together with the tops and bark of and belonging to the said one hundred trees hereby sold. And the said John Jones doth covenant, promise, and agree to and with the said William Burns, by these presents, that at all, or any time or times, until the day of in the year of our Lord he, the said William Burns, shall and may have. free liberty of ingress, egress, and regress, into and from all or any part of the lands and grounds belonging to the farm aforesaid, with horses, carts, and wagons, to take, fell, cut down, and carry away the said one hundred trees, and the tops and bark thereto, to and for his own use; and like liberty to dig saw-pits in convenient places in the said grounds, and therein to saw, cut out, and convert all, or so many of the said trees as he or they shall think fit, for the better conveniency or carriage thereof. And the said William Burns doth covenant, promise, and agree, to and with the said John Jones, by these presents, as followeth that is to say, that within the time aforesaid, he, the said William Burns, will choose out, and at his own charge fell, cut down, and carry away, the said one hundred trees so sold to him as aforesaid; and in consideration and in full for the purchase thereof, shall and will truly pay, or cause to be paid, unto the said John Jones, in addition to the sum of fifty dollars already paid, the receipt whereof is acknowledged above, the further sum of fifty dollars, in the manner following, viz: part thereof on the next ensuing the date of these presents, and the remaining sum of on the next following.

This agreement is to be binding as well upon and in favor of the executors, administrators, and assigns, of both parties, as the parties themselves.

2. The date of the first public performance shall be the- day of

3. The Manager agrees, as compensation for services hereunder, to pay the Actor the sum of $ - every week from the date of the first public performance of the play. 

4. (a) The Actor, if required, shall give four weeks' rehearsal without pay; if further rehearsals are required, then for each additional week or part thereof, the Manager shall pay the Actor full salary therefor. (b) Rehearsals shall be considered to be continuous from the date of the first rehearsal to the date of the first public performance of the play as provided in paragraph two. (c) If the above play is a musical play, or a spectacular production, then, wherever the word "Four" appears with reference to rehearsals in this contract, the word "Five" shall be substituted. 

5. This contract may before the beginning of rehearsals be terminated as follows:

If this contract be signed and entered into prior to two months of the date mentioned in paragraph two: (a) By either party give the other written notice and making payment of a sum equal to two weeks' salary. 

This contract may, during rehearsals, be terminated as follows and not otherwise: (b) At any time during the first ten days' rehearsals of the Actor by either party giving written notice, if this contract be signed and entered into within two months 9

of the date mentioned in paragraph two, except in case the Actor be reëngaged for a part which he has previously played; or (c) At any time after the first ten days' rehearsals of the Actor, by the Manager, by paying the Actor a sum equal to two weeks' salary. (d) The Actor may cancel the contract by giving written notice and paying to the Manager a sum equal to two weeks' salary. (e) If a play be rehearsed less than ten days and abandoned by the Manager, the Manager shall pay the Actor one weeks' salary. 

6. Either party may terminate this contract at any time on or after the date of the first public performance of the play by giving the other party two weeks' written notice. 

7. (a) If the play runs four weeks or less, the Manager may close the play and company without notice, and terminate the right of the Actor to further compensation, except as hereafter provided, provided he has paid the Actor for all services rendered from the date of the first public performance, and in no event less than two weeks' salary. Should the A. E. A. consent, the Manager may reopen the play during the current season, which event he shall offer the Actor a reëngagement under this form of contract upon the same terms and upon acceptance by the Actor enter into with the Actor such contract of reengagement. Should the Manager fail to do this or reopen the play without the consent of the A. E. A., the previous terms of this clause shall not apply to the Actor and Clause 6 shall remain in full force. (b) If the play shall run more than four weeks, the

Manager shall give one weeks' notice of the closing of the season of the play and company, and thereby terminate the right of the Actor to compensation except for services performed to the date of closing pursuant to such notice.

EMPLOYMENT 

259 8. If the Manager is prevented from giving rehearsals because of fire, accident, riot, strikes, illness of star, or prominent member of the cast, Act of God, public enemy or any other cause which could not reasonably be anticipated, or prevented, then the time so lost shall not be counted as part of the four weeks' rehearsal period herein provided. When said time so lost shall exceed two weeks, the Actor shall be free if he so elects. 

9. (a) The Actor shall furnish and pay for such clothes as are customarily worn by civilians of the present day in this country, together with wigs, boots, and shoes necessarily appurtenant thereto. All other clothes, wigs, shoes, costumes and appurtenances and all "properties" of the actress shall be furnished by the Manager. (b) If the Actor be a woman, then the following clause supersedes (a):

In both dramatic and musical companies all gowns, hats and all properties of the actress shall be furnished by the Manager. Footwear and wigs for modern plays to be furnished by the Actress. (c) It is understood that in every case where the Manager furnished costumes and appurtenances under this paragraph of the agreement, if notice of cancellation of this contract be given by such Actor, in that event he or she shall reimburse the Manager for the necessary and reasonable expense to which Manager may be put in altering or rearranging such costumes for his or her successor. 

10. (a) Eight performances shall constitute a week's work. A sum equal to one-eighth of the weekly salary shall be paid for each performance over eight in each week. 

(b) Salaries shall be paid on Saturday night. 

11. The Manager hereby agrees to transport at his expense the Actor when required to travel, including transportation from Philadelphia, to the opening point, and back to Philadelphia, from the closing point; also

the Actor's personal baggage up to two hundred pound weight. 

12 (a) If this contract is cancelled by the Manager, he agrees to pay the railroad fare of the actor back to Philadelphia. (b) If this contract is cancelled by the Actor, he agrees to pay his own railroad fare back to Philadelphia, and to reimburse the Manager for any railroad fare the Manager may have to pay for the Actor's successor up to an amount not exceeding railroad fare from Philadelphia to the point where said successor joins the Comrany. (c) If the Company is organized and its members are engaged outside of Philadelphia, the names of such place is, unless otherwise stated, herein agreed to be substituted for Philadelphia in paragraphs eleven and twelve. 

13. The Actor shall travel with the Company by such routes as the Manager may direct, and the Actor shall not demand compensation for any performance lost through unavoidable delay in travel which prevents such performance by the Company. 

14. It is further agreed that if the Company cannot perform because of fire, accident, strikes, riot, act of God, the public enemy, or for any other cause which could not be reasonably anticipated or prevented, or if the Actor cannot perform or rehearse on account of illness or any other valid reason, then the Actor shall not be entitled to any salary for the time during which said services shall not for such reason or reasons be rendered. 

If this illness of the Actor should continue for a period of ten days or more, the Manager may terminate the contract. 

15. The Actor agrees to be prompt at rehearsals, to pay strict regard to make-up and dress, to perform his services in a competent and painstaking manner, to abide by all reasonable rules and regulations, and to render services exclusively to the Manager from the date of the

EMPLOYMENT 

261 beginning of rehearsals, and shall not render services to any other person, firm or corporation, without the consent of the Manager. 

16. All communications which refer to the Company in general shall be posted upon the call-board. Notice to the Manager must be given to him personally or to his representatives. 

17. The Manager agrees that (1) all actors in the company in which the actor is herein employed and (2) all actors in any company in which any member of the A. E. A. is employed and which the Manager individually, or as a co-partner, or through a corporation shall continue throughout the term hereof to be members in good standing of the Actor's Equity Association. In case of a breach hereof the Actor may terminate this agreement forthwith, in which case the Manager agrees to pay the 

Actor all sums due to date of termination, plus his return fare and plus, as liquidated damages (no present basis for calculation existing a sum equal to two weeks' salary. 

18. In event any dispute shall arise between the parties as to any matter or thing covered by this contract, then said dispute or claim shall be arbitrated. The Manager shall choose one arbitrator and the Actor's Equity Association the second. If within three days these arbitrators shall not be able to agree, then, within that time they shall choose a third, who shall not in any way be connected with the theatrical profession. 

If they fail to do so, J. S., or his appointee shall be the third. The arbitrators shall hear the parties and within ten days decide the dispute or claim. 

The decision of a majority of said arbitrators shall be the decision of all, and shall be binding; and said decision shall be final.

The arbitrators shall determine by whom and in what proportion the cost of the arbitration shall be paid. The parties hereby appoint said Board its agents, with full power to finally settle said dispute or claim, and agree

that its decision shall constitute an agreement between them, having the same binding force as if agreed to by the parties themselves.

Should suit be brought before the selection of arbitrators, the party sued may (unless he shall have previously refused arbitration at the request of the other party, or neglected to accept same when tendered) at any time after suit and before trial give notice to arbitrate, and then in such case, arbitrators must be chosen as stated hereinabove.

E. Agreement for the Working of a Farm AGREEMENT made the tween John Jones of day of Township, 19-, be- County,

Penna. of one part, and David Dutton of the same place, of the other part. WHEREAS, the said John Jones is the owner of a farm in the Township aforesaid, and the said Dutton is about to move upon and work the same, Now 

IN RELATION THERETO IT IS HEREBY MUTUALLY AGREED, as follows: 

1. The said Dutton is to live in the house on said farm and is not to take any other family than his own to live with him or in the house; he is to provide his own fuel, and is not to use any from the farm without the consent of said Jones, which, if given, will be in consideration of some return to be rendered therefor. 

He is to cultivate the said farm in a husbandmanlike

manner; to put in, work, harvest and thresh the crops in good season, and to do all work necessary in marketing the same. He is to furnish his own horses, wagons, ploughs, and all other tools, implements and machinery for carrying on the farming and work connected therewith, and to pay all bills and expenses for keeping the same in repair; he is to keep the fences generally in repair, and is to make such new fences as may be needed, not exceeding fifty panels, the materials for which are to be furnished by said Jones. 

2. The said Jones is to pay all taxes assessed on the farm, and he is to furnish a sufficient stock of cows, hogs and poultry, which stock is to be kept good, that is, of equal value, from the proceeds of the farm. At the expiration of this agreement, said stock to be valued or sold; and one-half of the excess over cost to be allowed and paid to said Dutton. 

3. Each party to pay for one-half of the seed grain, grass seeds, and also feed if any shall be necessarily bought for the stock. 

4. As many cows to be kept as the farm will profitably bear; in summer not to be overstocked; in winter enough to consume the hay and fodder raised. Dutton's horses as above to be fed from the produce of farm. No hay, straw, corn-fodder, or manure to be sold or removed from the farm. 

5. Each party to have as many potatoes and as much garden produce and fruit (if grown), as he may require for use in his own family. 

6. The produce of the farm, not consumed as aforesaid, to be sold. The property in said produce until sold to be and remain in said Jones. The sales thereof to be by him or subject to his approval and direction. The money therefor to be paid to and received by him; when so received he shall deduct from the same such sums as he may have paid for common expenses under this agreement, and pay over one-half of the remainder to said

EMPLOYMENT 

267 Dutton. Settlements of said receipts and expenses to be made monthly. The possession of the farm to be and remain in said Jones, except so far as may be necessary in carrying on the farming operation by Dutton in pursuance of this agreement. 

7. This agreement to continue for one year from the day of next, and thereafter from year to year; but either party may terminate the same at the expiration of the first or any subsequent year, by giving notice to the other party of his intention so to do, months previous to the expiration of the then current year.

Articles of agreement made and conducted the day of

The said John Jones, for the considerations hereinafter mentioned, doth hereby covenant and agree to and with the said William Burns, in manner following, to wit: 

That he, the said John Jones, from the day of the date hereof, for and during the full term of three years, if they the said John Jones and William Burns shall both so long live, shall and will at the now dwelling-house of him, the said William Burns, situated in Reading aforesaid, or at such other place or places, (if by him the said William Burns, from time to time so required, ordered, and directed), work as a journeyman, and well and truly and faithfully serve him the said William Burns, in the business of a millwright, carpenter, joiner, turner, and in all such other arts, mysteries, and work as he, the said John Jones now is, or shall be anywise capable of doing or performing, during the term aforesaid, and that according to the best of his the said John Jones, ability,

knowledge, and judgment therein; and that he, the said 

John Jones, during the continuance of the said term, shall yearly work and perform the trade or business aforesaid for him, the said William Burns, in manner as follows, viz: from the twenty-second day of March to the twenty-second day of September, from the hour of six in the morning to six in the evening, and from the twenty-second day of September to the twenty-second day of March, from daylight to daylight, and that daily, (sickness, Sundays, Christmas, New Year's day, the fourth day of July, and such days as he may be lawfully required to muster as a militia-man, and usual hours of breakfast and dinner and supper, only allowed and excepted). And further, that he, the said John Jones, during the term aforesaid, shall not at any time absent himself from such service of the said William Burns, nor work, do, or perform any part of the said trade or business aforesaid, for the use or benefit of any other person or persons whomsoever, without the consent of the said Burns first had in writing for that purpose. And the said William Burns doth hereby covenant, promise, and agree to and with the said John Jones, that he, the said William Burns, shall and will well and truly pay, or cause to be paid unto the said John Jones, for his said services, the sum of forty dollars per month, and board him during the said time. 

Witness our hands and seals, etc.

8. CLAUSES Clause Permitting Delivery Within Specified Time after Due Date 

Goods shipped within three weeks after specified time of delivery shall constitute good delivery.

Clause Governing Extension of Time for Delivery in 

Absence of Shipping Instructions

There shall be no extension of time [s] of shipment [s] specified under this contract except as herein provided for, or as hereafter mutually agreed upon in writing; provided that in case of the Buyer's failure to furnish, at least fifteen (15) days before the expiration of contract time of shipment, shipping instructions for shipment within the remaining period of contract time of shipment, and if in such case the seller does not mail or telegraph, at any time on or before the expiration date of the contract time of shipment, notice to the buyer at the buyer's address above given that the seller elects to hold the buyer for breach of contract, then this contract shall be automatically extended as to all the above commodities then unshipped for an additional period of thirty (30) days from the expiration of contract time of shipment.

Clause Permitting Buyer to Fix Place of Delivery 

All merchandise shall be delivered f. o. b., or at warehouse at , as may be specified by the buyer. 

Clause Governing Delivery to Consignee Where Freight Is Prepaid by Consignor 

Delivery at place of shipment to carrier, duly consigned, shall constitute delivery to consignee, and prepayment of freight by Company shall not alter this provision, since prepayment of freight is made solely for the convenience of the consignee. 

Clause Indicating That Time of Delivery Is of the 

Essence

Delivery at the time specified in this contract shall be considered as of the essence of the agreement.

Clause Providing for Cancellation upon Failure to Deliver 

Upon failure of the seller to deliver any installment within thirty days from the due date of delivery of such installment, the buyer may, by notifying the seller, in writing within five days after the expiration of such thirty days, cancel all remaining undelivered installments, unless default in delivery is due to conditions beyond the control of the seller as set forth above. 

Clause Providing Optional Remedies for the Buyer upon 

Failure of Seller to Deliver 

That if the seller shall fail, for reasons other than fires, strikes, breakdowns, labor difficulties, acts of carriers, or any causes beyond the control of the seller, to make any shipment on or before the expiration of contract time of shipment when shipping instructions are received by the seller at least fifteen (15) days before the expiration date of contract time of shipment, or shall fail, in case of an extension hereof, to make any shipment on or before the extended time of shipment when shipping instructions are received by the seller at least fifteen (15) days before the expiration date of extended time of shipment, then the buyer may, at its option, give written notice to the seller that the buyer elects to treat the seller's failure to make shipment as a breach of this contract, and in case such notice is received by the seller before actual shipment the seller shall be liable to the buyer for breach of contract and shall pay to the buyer on demand any loss to the buyer represented by the difference between the contract price of the commodities to be shipped or delivered and the market price thereof at the time of seller's breach (it being understood that the market price of said commodities at the time of seller's breach is seller's list price in effect at such time

for said commodities delivered f. o. b., at the same point and with freight charges added at the same rate per cwt. as provided under the paragraph marked "prices" on the front of this contract). In the event the buyer does not elect to treat such failure on the part of the seller as a breach of contract, by written notice received by the seller at any time before shipment, this contract shall be extended so as to include the shipment and delivery when made; provided that the buyer, however, shall be entitled to a credit of ten cents (10c) per barrel on flour and fifty cents (50c) per ton on feed for each thirty-days period of delay or fractional part there until shipment is made.

Cause Requiring Notice of Inability to Deliver 

Whenever the seller is unable to make delivery due to the occurrence of any of the contingencies above mentioned, he shall notify the buyer within ten days, after he has knowledge thereof.

Clause Requiring Delivery after Removal of Disability 

If the seller is unable to make delivery at the time specified by reason of fires, strikes, floods, failure of transportation facilities, or for any cause the condition beyond the seller's control, such inability shall not in any wise invalidate this contract, but the seller shall make delivery within thirty days from the termination of the cause or condition responsible for the seller's inability to deliver.

AMICABLE ACTION SEE JUDGMENTS 

There is, in Pennsylvania, a mode of instituting suits without a service by sheriff, by an amicable agreement, signed by the parties or their attorneys, and filed in the prothonotary's office. 

When entered such action is considered as if it had been adversely commenced, and the defendant had been regularly summoned. It saves the expense of the original writ, and the sheriff's fee for serving it. The writ, however, is supposed in law to be filed. A case may be stated for the opinion of the court in this way, or a judgment entered. When a judgment is entered in this way, the cause of action should always be expressed in the agreement, and it is well that it be attested by two witnesses.

ARBITRATION AND REFERENCE 

An arbitration is the reference and submission of a matter in dispute, concerning property or a personal wrong, to the decision of one or more persons as arbitrators. Their findings are called awards.

Arbitrations are either voluntary or compulsory. The voluntary are those made by mutual consent; and the compulsory are where either party has a right to enter a rule of reference without the consent of the other. Before the revised Act of 1836, a variety of modes of arbitration existed in Pennsylvania. 1st.

Are those made by mutual consent, in which the parties select the arbitrators, and bind themselves by bond to abide their decision; these are made without any rule of court. 3 Bl. Com. 

16. 2d. Those which are made in a cause pending in court by a rule of court, before trial; these are arbitrations at common law, and the award is enforced by attachment. Kyd on Awards

HEAD-NOTE 

309 21. 3d. Those which are made by virtue of the statute 9 & 10 

Will. 3, c. 15, by which it is agreed to refer a matter in dispute, not then in court, to arbitrators, and agree that the submission. be made a rule of court, which is enforced as if it had been made a rule of court. Kyd on Awards 22. 4th. Those made under the Act of Assembly of 1705. 

The provisions of the Acts of 1705 and 1810, and the English statutes above mentioned, have been incorporated into the revised Act of 1836. The methods of arbitration at this time most usual in Pennsylvania, are those made by mutual consent, in which the parties select the arbitrators, and bind themselves by bond to abide their decision; or those under the Act of Assembly of 16th June, 1836, P. L. 717, 1 Purd. 342 et seq., which provides for either voluntary or compulsory arbitrations. Either party, in a civil suit or action, or his attorney, may enter at the Prothonotary's office, a rule of reference under the said Act. of 1836, wherein he shall declare his determination to have arbitrators chosen on a certain day to be mentioned therein, not exceeding thirty days thereafter, for the trial of all matters in variance in the suit between the parties; provided, that the plaintiff shall not enter such rule until he files a declaration or statement of his cause of action. A copy of this rule is to be served on the opposite party, his agent or attorney, at least fifteen days before the day fixed for the appointment of arbitrators. On the day appointed they meet at the Prothonotary's, and endeavor to agree upon arbitrators; if they cannot, the 

Prothonotary makes out a list on which are inscribed the names of a number of citizens, and the parties, beginning with the plaintiff, alternately strike one of said names at a time from the list, until there are left but the number agreed upon or fixed by the Prothonotary, who are to be the arbitrators. The time of meeting is then agreed upon by the parties, or appointed by the Prothonotary, provided that the time of meeting shall not be less than ten nor more than twenty days after their appointment. 

The party by whom the rule of reference shall have been entered must procure from the Prothonotary a certified copy of the record, and serve a copy of the same on each of the arbitrators, and also on the opposite party, his agent or attorney, giving ten days' notice previous to the day of meeting. At the time. fixed for the meeting, the arbitrators are sworn or affirmed, justly and equitably to try all matters in variance submitted to them,

and proceed to hear and determine the case. Their award is filed in the office of the Prothonotary, and has the effect of a judgment, subject, however, to an appeal, which may be entered at any time within twenty days after the filing of such award. 

There is no compulsory arbitration in the City and County of Philadelphia. 

By the Act of May 14th, 1874, P. L. 166, 4 Purd. 4068 et seq., all civil suits or cases which the parties may legally by agreement in writing submit to the decision of a Court, the parties may, in like manner, by written agreement, submit the case to the decision of any person learned in the law, who is authorized to act as an attorney in the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania. 

The Act of April 25th, 1927, P. L. 381, et seq., provides that a provision in any written contract, except a contract for personal services, to arbitrate any controversy thereafter arising out of the contract or out of the refusal to perform the whole or any part thereof, or a written agreement to submit to arbitration any controversy existing at the time of the agreement to arbitrate, shall be valid, irrevocable and enforceable. The 

Court on application shall stay any proceedings brought in violation of the arbitration agreement. The act provides the procedure in case one party refuses to proceed with the arbitration agreement. If the making of the arbitration agreement or the failure, neglect or refusal to perform the same, is raised as an issue, the Court, if a jury trial is waived, or the jury, shall try the issue, otherwise all other matters in dispute shall be decided in accordance with the arbitration agreement.

ARREST IN CIVIL CASES CAPIAS AD RESPONDENDUM 

The Capias ad respondendum is an old common law writ used widely by creditors in order to imprison worthless debtors. By the Act of 1842, however, its scope was greatly limited. It can issue only in (1) actions ex delicto, (2) proceedings for contempt, (3) for fines and penalties, (4) for breach of promise to marry, (5) for moneys collected by public officers or for misconduct in office or profession. The writ is original process issued like a summons upon the filing of an affidavit to hold to bail. 

The defendant is taken by the sheriff bodily and may either give bond or move to quash or abate. Married women, ambassadors, etc., witnesses, infants, and freeholders (see 22 C. C. 77) are exempt from capias.

Special Capias may issue after suit begun (Act of 1836 P. L. 

573).

(Caption.) 

PRÆCIPE TO THE PROTHO NOTARY, C. P. 

Sir: Issue Capias ad Respondendum returnable the first Monday of December, 1929. Bail allowed $ Date. 

Attorney for plaintiff.

CAPIAS AD SATISFACIENDUM 

The writ of capias ad satisfaciendum is a final process issued after entry of judgment. Since it involves the incarceration of the defendant, its use has been limited to cases which could have been begun by capias (Act of 1842, P. L. 339). Where the suit was begun by summons, execution will generally issue both in fieri facias and capias resp. at the same time. (As to discharge from arrest because of the insolvency of the debtor under the 

Act of 1915, P. L. 704, see infra.)
